subject: Throughput & SLO follow-up: Acme streaming + QPS clarification
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput & SLO follow-up: Acme streaming + QPS clarification

Hi Jordan / Sophie —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the follow-ups we discussed so we can size a proposal: 

What we heard / current targets
- Primary use case: in-chat streaming responses with partial tokens returned as they are generated (low-latency interactive).
- Latency SLO: p95 end-to-end generation latency target ~350ms (client observed).
- Steady-state QPS: roughly 120 requests/sec (from product dashboards) — this is the steady baseline.
- Average tokens per request (round-trip): I estimated ~80 tokens earlier; please confirm.
- Peak/burst profile: up to ~500-700 req/sec for short bursts (30-120s) during marketing pushes.
- Concurrency: estimated streaming concurrency ~250 active streams during peaks.

Preliminary capacity numbers (rough):
- Steady tokens/sec = 120 req/s * 80 tokens = 9,600 tokens/sec (please confirm tokens per request).
- Peak tokens/sec (700 req/s * 80 tokens) = 56,000 tokens/sec.

What we need from you to finalize sizing
1) Confirm average tokens per request (you can break down: user prompt tokens vs model response tokens).
2) Representative 24-48h traffic distribution or a sample telemetry CSV (timestamps, req_id, request_tokens, response_tokens).
3) Clarify whether the client-side SLO is measured from click->first-byte or end->end latency; streaming first-byte SLOs are easier to hit than full completion time.

Next steps
- I attached a short throughput template (redwood-throughput-template.xlsx) — please fill and return.
- Once we get the telemetry + tokens per request, we’ll run a short sizing pass and propose 2 options (hosted autoscale and dedicated reserved capacity) with estimated monthly cost and recommended GPU pools.
- Propose a 30-minute follow-up next week with our SEs to review findings — what’s your availability?

Attachments: redwood-throughput-template.xlsx (template for traffic/token breakdown)

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput & SLO follow-up: Acme streaming + QPS clarification

Thanks Rafael — good notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Tokens per request: on average our user prompt is ~50 tokens and the model returns ~180 tokens (so ~230 tokens total per request). We missed that breakdown earlier — apologies.
- Steady-state QPS: our telemetry shows ~100 QPS over the last month (60-120 range depending on region).
- Peak/bursts: we have seen spikes up to ~700 QPS for ~90s during a campaign last quarter. We should plan for that profile.
- Streaming behavior: yes, we stream partial tokens as generated and our SLO is measured as first-byte for the streaming response (we still care about completion time for UX but first-byte is the critical metric).
- Concurrency: active streaming connections reached ~400 during the biggest spike, but more commonly 150-300.

I’m attaching a small telemetry extract (acme-telemetry-sample.csv) with timestamps and token counts — should help with the initial calc. Let me know if you need a larger window.

On the call, you mentioned p95 <= 350ms first-byte — that sounds like a reasonable target but please advise on what that implies for instance sizing given our token counts above.

Cheers,
Jordan
Jordan Miller
Director of Product — Conversational AI | Acme Corp
jordan.miller@acme.com

On Wed, Apr 28, 2027 at 3:12 PM Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Jordan / Sophie —
> 
> Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the follow-ups we discussed so we can size a proposal: 
>

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput & SLO follow-up: Acme streaming + QPS clarification

Jordan — great, that token breakdown is super helpful. Updated quick math below based on your numbers: 

- Steady-state tokens/sec = 100 req/s * 230 tokens = 23,000 tokens/sec.
- Peak tokens/sec = 700 req/s * 230 tokens = 161,000 tokens/sec.
- Streaming first-byte SLO (p95 <= 350ms) is measured client-side — that means our sizing will favor lower-latency instance profiles and lower batch sizes for the model.

Prelim recommendations 
- Given heavy streaming and first-byte SLOs, dedicated pools (reserved capacity) are usually a safer bet for predictable latency, especially if you want to avoid cold-start variability during bursts. We’ll model both hosted autoscale and a dedicated baseline plus burst capacity.
- For initial sizing, we’ll run a short performance pass: replay your telemetry on our staging environment against the model variant you plan to use and capture p50/p95 first-byte and completion times. Can you confirm the model name/variant and whether you plan to use quantized weights?

Next steps (concrete):
1) SE sizing call — 30 min to confirm model variant and run through telemetry. Suggested slots: Mon 5/3 09:30-10:00 PT or Tue 5/4 11:00-11:30 PT. Which works?
2) You’ll send a longer telemetry dump (24-72h) if possible; we’ll replay and return a short report.
3) We’ll provide 2 pricing/architecture options with estimated monthly cost and expected p95 first-byte under steady and peak loads.

Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2027-042 (I’ve recorded the ask)

Thanks — I’ll loop in our infra SEs on the follow-up once you confirm a slot.

Best,
Rafael
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 08:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput & SLO follow-up: Acme streaming + QPS clarification (internal)

Looping internally — Rafael, I’ll put together two draft options after the SE sizing run:
- Option A: Hosted autoscale with burst credits and priority routing (lower upfront, slightly higher unit cost).
- Option B: Dedicated reserved pool sized for steady-state + a burst pool (higher commit, lower steady unit cost).

I’ll aim to have preliminary numbers and an SE runbook by Monday morning PT. Neha — can you own scheduling the SE run and confirming available infra slots?

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
